title: Page header
summary: The top of a page, a section or a record: a breadcrumb row, a title bar with actions, and a note line. Stacks by its own width, with the actions full width and touch-sized on a phone.

props.name: heading
props.description: The title. Without it (and without default or actions content) the title bar is not shown.

props.name: level
props.description: The heading level the title exposes to assistive technology (aria-level).

props.name: variant
props.description: page is the standard page top; section is a titled section inside a page (title, actions, note); record is the compact strip of a single-record page (chips on the left, actions right).

props.name: sticky
props.description: Pins the header to the top of the scrolling page body while the content scrolls: in pk-app-shell flush under the app bar (the body is the scroller), in a plain page at the top of the viewport.

slots.description: Beside the title: status chips, badges or your own heading element.

slots.name: breadcrumb
slots.description: A pk-breadcrumb (or any trail) above the title; hidden when empty.

slots.name: actions
slots.description: Buttons at the right of the title bar; full width and touch-sized on a narrow container.

slots.name: meta
slots.description: A note or metadata line under the title bar; hidden when empty.

parts.name: titlebar
parts.description: The row holding the title and the actions.

parts.name: lead
parts.description: The title and the default slot.

cssProperties.name: --pk-page-header-sticky-top
cssProperties.description: Offset from the top of the scroller when sticky. 0 is flush under the app bar inside pk-app-shell; on a plain page under a fixed bar of your own set it to that bar's height (for example var(--app-header-h)).

a11y: The header is a header element, not a banner landmark, so it is safe inside main. The title is exposed as a heading whose level you choose with level, so it fits the page outline (use 1 for a page, 2 or 3 for a section). Give the breadcrumb slot a pk-breadcrumb, which is its own labelled navigation landmark.
